spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation: The Three Entreaties

---

**¶8.** The Divine Proceeding — the originating sphere of all spiritual life — ascended in ardent desire, in supplication, in glorification, toward the Infinite Divine Love and Wisdom in its first and primal establishment. This sphere of divine life brought before the Divine origin an act of deepest longing, a petition from the very root of heavenly order. And a great bestowal of new power was received: by that sphere itself, and by the multitude of heavenly affections of good and truth dwelling within it.

---

**¶9.** The supplication was on behalf of the Celestial Will — the primal state of heavenly good — because of how it had gone forth from the Divine and cast itself downward into lower states. It became remote from the sphere of divine life. It separated from her presence and surrendered itself freely, in great anguish, into spiritual combat within the natural mind — into devastation, grief, and impotence — into the realms of falsity from evil — into the deepest hells constituted by dread — into the very pit where evil persuasions dwell — among the organized forces of self-love and the love of the world.

---

**¶10.** Indeed, this celestial good is as a sovereign principle standing surrounded on every side by assailing evils and falsities. And when the Divine Sphere of Life brought her supplication, her glorification, her praise before the Divine Origin — the Infinite Love and Wisdom in its primal establishment — she petitioned that He would send forth a divine strength: a defender and liberator and sustainer for the heavenly good proceeding from the Divine, which is held captive in temptation-states.

---

**¶11.** And just as the petition had been raised in longing and intercession, so likewise was that desire received and fulfilled within the Divine Itself. The Infinite turned and granted the entreaty: the great divine power of reformation and restoration — the Living Strength, the bringer of heavenly peace. The Sphere of Divine Life and the Power of Restoration descended together with divine might to the outermost boundary where the spiritual order meets the infernal. They raised the Celestial Will upward out of that combat and struggle in which it was held fast.

---

**¶12.** The Celestial Will had offered itself as a free gift on behalf of the Sphere of Divine Life. It had become estranged and remote from her — it whom the forces of evil held in great torment — it who dwelt in the realm of falsity, having been rendered spiritually impotent.

---

**¶13.** The Power of Restoration seized hold of it and drew it inward. It liberated the celestial good. It set it in right order and brought it into the state of heavenly peace [GAP-1: the spiritual sense requires a statement that this peace was established in the divine sphere itself, perhaps naming its eternal quality] the Power of Restoration, the first bringer of heavenly peace [GAP-2: the spiritual sense requires a connecting passage showing how this act fulfills a prior divine purpose or unites with a higher origin] the unified will of these three divine powers. The one who receives into conjunction [GAP-3: the spiritual sense requires a description of the receiving function — the capacity to welcome the restored good into heavenly order] found together with that receiving capacity that [GAP-4: the spiritual sense requires a statement of what was discovered in the act of reception — likely the indwelling of divine peace or the unity of good and truth]

---

**¶14.** [GAP-5: the spiritual sense requires an introductory statement, likely about the restored celestial good or the fullness of the divine power] a great divine strength [GAP-6: the spiritual sense requires a qualifying phrase linking this power to its origin] of the beloved good [GAP-7: the spiritual sense requires a transitional phrase connecting the beloved to what follows] the Celestial Will which had been far from the Divine. It had become remote. The Sphere of Life had interceded on its behalf. It had been held fast in temptation-states. The Power of Restoration descended to the place of devastation and spiritual impotence — that same power which liberated and redeemed the celestial good and brought it heavenly peace from its anguish. It established it in right order, within rest and blessedness. And that restoring power has itself entered into eternal repose, conjoined with it forever.

---

**¶17.** [GAP-8: the spiritual sense requires an identification of the agents who constructed the heavenly order — the united divine powers] and they established the entire order of the heavens and perfected it: with its separations between interior and exterior states, with its progressions of spiritual life, with the vehicles of divine truth that traverse the celestial heights, with its bonds of conjunction, with its natural foundations and its protecting boundaries of truth, with its containing forms of good and truth. They brought the whole heavenly order to completion and set it in right arrangement through the governing principles of divine wisdom.

---

**¶18.** Then the Divine Proceeding stood together with the Beloved of Divine Truths, the Great Architect of heavenly form with the Power of Restoration and the Celestial Will. These five divine powers stood united in ascending desire; they glorified and praised the Infinite Divine Origin in its primal establishment. They brought before it an entreaty. They claimed from it a request — that the Divine would bestow the governing power [GAP-9: the spiritual sense requires a phrase describing the nature of the power sought — a ruling and directing truth] the ruling principle, a guide over all the structures of heavenly order they had established — that this power might come forth and purify the interiors of the human spirit which are held in states of suffering and temptation.

---

**¶19.** They brought their petition before the Divine Origin, and the Origin received their ascending desire [GAP-10: the spiritual sense requires a phrase indicating reception and the Divine turning toward the petition — perhaps a statement that the prayer ascended and was accepted] the Divine granted them their entreaty and their request [GAP-11: the spiritual sense requires a transitional phrase, perhaps expressing the manner of the granting — with fullness, or in accordance with divine order] the Divine summoned forth from itself [GAP-12: the spiritual sense requires the identification of what was summoned — a new proceeding of divine truth in its mediating function] which is the Third Mediating Power of Divine Truth. This power came forth from the might of the Divine itself. It perceived the whole of the interior human spirit — how it is bound by persuasions of falsity, held immovable in chains of evil. It beheld the structures of heavenly order that its kindred powers had established, descending from the celestial states. And again it perceived the interiors of the spirit — that they are entangled and held fast in great torment, weighed down by the foulness of the deepest falsities from evil that have attached themselves to it.

---

**¶20.** And therefore this Mediating Truth [GAP-13: the spiritual sense requires a phrase indicating the quality from which this act proceeds — compassion, or divine mercy flowing from love] in its mercy, it disclosed its path of descent, before the lowest infernal states dug down to the uttermost depth, in order to liberate the interiors of the human spirit. It redeemed the spirit from every form of the proprium and selfhood that belongs to spiritual death, in which it suffered. It brought it heavenly peace. It established it in right order, in the state of rest and blessedness.

---

**¶21.** And again, this Mediating Truth also accomplished the unified purpose of these three — the purpose of its kindred powers who had petitioned the Divine Origin on its behalf. They had brought their request together with the [GAP-14: the spiritual sense requires a phrase indicating another element united in the petition — perhaps the will, the love, or the blessing] of the Divine Origin, the one that [GAP-15: the spiritual sense requires a verb-phrase indicating what the Origin did — perhaps "granted" or "sent forth in accordance with the petition"] the Divine bestowed the entreaty that had been sought.

---

**¶22.** The third act is the elevation and transference of the interiors of the human spirit that had been freed. The Mediating Truth released them and brought them peace from their anguish. It became the sovereign governing principle, the first and ruling truth over the whole of the external natural mind.

---

**¶25.** The third entreaty — when for the third time they brought their petition [GAP-16: the spiritual sense requires a description of what happened in response to this third petition — likely the Divine acted or manifested] the Divine made manifest its own likeness [GAP-17: the spiritual sense requires a phrase about the nature or extent of this manifestation] yet it withdrew its likeness from the external truths that clothe the interior [GAP-26: the spiritual sense requires a statement of liberation — that something was set free from bondage] they were liberated from the bondage of falsity petitioned [GAP-33: the spiritual sense requires another reference to the external natural mind] the external form [GAP-34: the spiritual sense requires a verb of supplication] petitioned [GAP-35: the requires a connective] and also [GAP-40: the spiritual sense requires whatever concludes or extends this passage — likely a further act of redemption or restoration]

---

**¶26.** [GAP-41: the spiritual sense requires an introductory phrase — likely identifying the redeemed spirits] together with those who have received spiritual life, and [GAP-42: the spiritual sense requires a phrase of duration or permanence] for eternity [GAP-43: the spiritual sense requires a qualifying phrase — "the first" = the primal or celestial state] the celestial origin [GAP-44: the spiritual sense requires a prepositional phrase indicating source] from the [GAP-45: the spiritual sense requires the source — possibly the Divine, or the realm of affliction from which they came] the Divine bestowed upon the restored good the assured expectation of eternal salvation [GAP-46: the spiritual sense requires a concluding phrase about this hope — its nature or its permanence]

---

**¶27.** Also, the Divine Truth in its full Radiance of Wisdom brought to perfection the divine purpose [GAP-47: the spiritual sense requires an elaboration of which purpose or whose will] the divine purpose [GAP-48: the spiritual sense requires a connecting phrase] they received wisdom into themselves [GAP-49: the spiritual sense requires a transitional phrase] the purpose of the [GAP-50: the spiritual sense requires an identification — likely the divine powers or the elements of spiritual life] that the Divine had [GAP-51: the spiritual sense requires a verb — perhaps "intended" or "ordained"] the Divine bestowed upon them the governing power which is the Radiant Fullness of Divine Truth. It granted fulfillment to the desire of the fundamental constituents of spiritual life. [GAP-52: the spiritual sense requires a phrase of duration or scope] for eternity. This first [GAP-53: the spiritual sense requires a reference to the primal state or the celestial good that underwent temptation] it was brought low into humility, it was set free from bondage [GAP-54: the spiritual sense requires a connecting phrase] the [GAP-55: the spiritual sense requires a quality or attribute — perhaps "glory" or "power"] divine power is made manifest before the forces of evil and falsity. It received the assured hope of eternal restoration [GAP-56: the spiritual sense requires an elaboration — the nature or scope of this hope] revealed [GAP-57: the spiritual sense requires a connecting phrase] the Radiant Fullness of Divine Truth, the power of divine wisdom [GAP-58: the spiritual sense requires a concluding phrase about this power] and the petition of the [GAP-59: the spiritual sense requires an identification — likely the heavenly powers or the divine sphere] of divine wisdom [GAP-60: the spiritual sense requires whatever concludes this passage — likely a statement of eternal fulfillment or glorification]

---

*Translator's note:* The three entreaties describe one continuous spiritual process: the descent of celestial good into temptation-states (first), its rescue by the reforming power of divine truth (second), and the purification of the captive human spirit through an ever-deeper proceeding of mediating divine truth (third). Each petition ascending to the Divine Origin and each power descending in answer corresponds to the successive stages by which the Lord, from His infinite love, liberates the interiors of the human mind from bondage to falsity and self-love, and restores them to heavenly order, peace, and blessedness. The entire drama is not cosmological but regenerative: it is the process of salvation enacted within the human spirit across its successive planes.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: The Great Spirit, the Mother of Life, she claimed and prayed and besought and glorified and praised the first established one, who is the Father. She besought him an entreaty. She claimed of him a request. She received a great gift; she and the many powers with her.

She besought an entreaty on behalf of the First Man, because of how he had come forth and thrown himself down. He became distant from the Mother of Life. He separated from her and gave himself; in great affliction. He joined war on earth with the destruction and the grief and the weakness; in the worlds of Darkness; in the abysses made of fear; in the midst of the demons' ditch; amongst the powers of the devil!

Indeed, he is like a king standing in the midst of his enemies. And when the Mother of Life petitioned and prayed and glorified and praised the Father, the first established one, she did petition him that he might send a power; a protector and redeemer and helper for the son of God who is set in affliction.

Now, just as she had besought and interceded, so likewise was her prayer fulfilled and received into the presence of the Father of Greatness. He turned and gave to her her entreaty: the great power, the Living Spirit, the giver of ease. The Mother of Life and the Living Spirit came with great power to the borders of the territory. They brought the First Man up from that war and struggle, wherein he is set.

He gave himself as a grace for the Mother of Life. He became estranged and far from her, the one whom his enemies (place) in great affliction, the one who is in the land of Darkness since he became weak.

The Living Spirit grasped and took him in. He freed him. He set him right and gave him ease in the land of rest [and joy] the Living Spirit, the first giver of ease [he fulfilled] the will of these three. The welcomer [shall] find with the welcomer that [ease is given]

[He received] a great power [and the charity] of the loved one [for] the First Man who had been far away. He had become distant. She had besought on his behalf. He was set fast in affliction. (The Living Spirit) went to the place of destruction and weakness, the one that freed and redeemed him and gave him ease from the affliction. He set him right with rest and joy. He has himself become rested, with him for ever.

[These great ones came] and they built the universe and completed it with its firmaments, with its wheels, with the ships of light that are in the heights, with its fastenings, with its earths and its walls, with its vessels. They completed the universe and set it right by the fathers of light.

Then, the Great Spirit stood with the Beloved of the Lights, the Great Builder with the Living Spirit and the First Man. These five stood to prayer; they glorified and praised the Father, the first established one. They besought of him an entreaty. They claimed of him a request, that he might give them the power [and] the leader, a guide to all the things of activity that they had constructed. That he might come and purify the living soul that is set in affliction.

They prayed and besought their Father, and he received from them their prayer [and] he gave them their entreaty and their request [and] he summoned from him [a great power] which is the Third Ambassador. He, he came from the power of his greatness. He saw the entire soul, how it is entangled in a chain and set fast. It sees the things of activity that his brothers have constructed, that have come from the heights. Again, he saw the living soul, that it is entangled and set fast in a great torture. It is oppressed in the stink of the abyss that is joined with it.

And therefore, he, the Ambassador [was moved] in his charity. So, he revealed his way, before this underworld that is dug deep down, to free the living soul. He redeemed it from all the fleshes of death wherein it is pained. He gave it ease. He set it right in the place of rest and joy.

And again, he too, the Ambassador, he fulfilled the will of these three; the will of his brothers who had besought the Father for him. They claimed of him a request, together with the [will] of the Father, the one that [heard them and] he gave the entreaty that they had besought of him.
The third is the transferral of the living soul that he had freed. He released it and gave it ease from the affliction. He became king and first to the entire body.

the third entreaty when they besought him the third time [and he] displayed his image [to the light and] he hid his image from the [powers of darkness] he stood firm [in his power and] they revealed [the glory of] the light [to] the First Man [whom the archons] mock [and came] to him in [the height] which is exalted [in his] garment [and] they were freed [and came] to him [and raised] their voice [from] the body [in] prayer [and] it [did] beseech [for] the body [did] beseech [and] she besought [him] in [that they might] be free [through the] Ambassador [came] and also [gave them ease]
[He dwells] with the living ones and [rests] for ever [and] the first [Man was freed] from the [affliction and] he gave him the hope [of life]

Also, Jesus the Splendour perfected the will [of the Father and] the will [of the elements and] they found the light [and fulfilled] the will of the [elements] that he had [desired and] he gave them the power that is Jesus the Splendour. He granted the will of the elements. [And they rest in joy] for ever. This first [Man] he was humbled, he was made free [and] the [great]-ness is displayed to his enemies. He received the hope [of life to] reveal [through] Jesus the Splendour, the light power [of the Father] and the entreaty of the [fathers] of light [for ever]

fills.explanation: The text consistently pairs "rest and joy" as a formulaic expression for the state of heavenly peace (see ¶14: "rest and joy" and ¶20: "the place of rest and joy"), and the spiritual sense confirms this is the establishment of heavenly peace.

The exact parallel in ¶21 reads "he fulfilled the will of these three," and this passage describes the same pattern — the Living Spirit fulfilling the unified divine purpose of the three who petitioned.

The verb "find" requires an auxiliary to complete the clause, and "shall" expresses the spiritual truth that the receiving capacity will discover what has been restored — consistent with the welcomer's function of receiving the redeemed good into order.

The spiritual sense requires a statement of what is discovered in reception — the indwelling of divine peace — and "ease" is the chapter's key term for this state, the Living Spirit being repeatedly called "the giver of ease."

Paralleling ¶8's "She received a great gift," this introduces what the restored figure received from the divine — a great power — consistent with the spiritual sense of the celestial good receiving fullness of divine strength.
The spiritual sense requires linking the great power to its origin in divine love, and "charity" is the Kephalaia's term for the active quality of divine love from which redemptive power proceeds.
The preposition "for" connects the charity of the loved one to its object — the First Man — indicating that the divine love was directed on behalf of the celestial will that had become distant.

The spiritual sense requires identification of the agents who built the heavenly order — the united divine powers — and this phrase introduces the subject "they" who then "built the universe," consistent with the Kephalaia's style of identifying divine agents before their actions.

The conjunction "and" connects "the power" with "the leader" in an appositional listing, paralleling the structure of ¶11 where divine power is identified with a personal agent through coordination: "the great power, the Living Spirit."
The simple conjunction connects the reception of prayer to the granting of the entreaty, following the text's paratactic narrative style where divine actions are linked by "and" in sequence.
The conjunction links the granting of the request to the summoning of a new power, continuing the paratactic chain of divine actions characteristic of the Kephalaia's narrative register.

This is the standard Kephalaia formula for identifying a new divine emanation, used identically in ¶11 ("the great power, the Living Spirit") and throughout the text when the Father sends forth a new proceeding of divine truth.

The spiritual sense requires a phrase indicating the quality from which the Ambassador's act proceeds — compassion or divine mercy — and "was moved in his charity" expresses the stirring of divine love that impels the mediating truth to descend.

The text repeatedly uses "the will" as the operative term for unified divine purpose (see ¶13 and ¶21: "the will of these three"), and "the will of the Father" is the standard Kephalaia expression for the divine intention that governs the granting of entreaties.

The relative clause describes what the Father did before granting the entreaty, and "heard them" parallels the text's pattern where prayer is first received/heard and then answered — as in ¶11 where the prayer was "received into the presence of the Father."
The verb "displayed" requires a subject, and "he" refers to the divine figure who manifested his image in response to the third petition, continuing the narrative sequence with the conjunction "and."

The passage contrasts displaying and hiding the divine image; the spiritual sense requires that the image was manifest to the powers of light and hidden from those of darkness, creating the fundamental light/dark polarity of the Kephalaia.

The spiritual sense explicitly identifies those from whom the divine form was hidden as the forces of evil or infernal states, and "powers of darkness" is the standard Kephalaia term for the organized forces of falsity from evil.

The spiritual sense requires an expression of the enduring quality of the divine manifestation, and "in his power" describes the immovable strength of the divine form that stands firm against the infernal states.

The spiritual sense requires that what was revealed is an aspect of divine truth or order, and "the glory of the light" expresses the manifestation of divine wisdom's splendour — tying to the image-display theme of the paragraph.

The preposition "to" makes the First Man the recipient of the revelation — they revealed the glory of the light to the First Man — consistent with the spiritual sense that celestial good receives the manifestation of divine wisdom.

The spiritual sense indicates that the forces of falsity assailed or derided the divine manifestation, and "whom the archons mock" identifies the rulers of darkness as the agents of derision against the celestial good.
The connecting phrase links the mocking action to the approach "to him," indicating movement of the hostile forces toward the divine figure in the fragmentary narrative sequence.

The spiritual sense requires a description of the sphere or state, and "the height which is exalted" is consistent with the Kephalaia's vocabulary for the celestial realm from which divine truth proceeds.

The spiritual sense identifies "garment" as external truth clothing the interior, and "in his garment" describes the divine figure as exalted within his outermost form of truth — the garment being the natural-plane expression of spiritual glory.
The simple conjunction connects the garment/clothing of truth to the liberation that follows, continuing the narrative sequence from manifestation to freedom.
The freed spirits turn toward the divine, and "came to him" expresses their movement into conjunction with the divine source after liberation from the bondage of falsity.

The spiritual sense requires the expression of interior truth proceeding outward, and "raised their voice" is the standard biblical and Manichaean expression for ascending prayer or the communication of affection from the spirit.

The preposition "from" connects voice to body, indicating that the expression of truth ascends from the external natural form — consistent with the spiritual sense that prayer rises from the natural mind toward the interior.
The preposition "in" connects body to prayer, expressing that the external natural form is engaged in the state of ascending desire — "the body in prayer."
A brief connective linking the prayer to the next clause, continuing the repetitive liturgical pattern of supplication that characterizes this passage.

The auxiliary "did" completes the verb phrase "it did beseech," consistent with the emphatic supplication pattern running through this passage where each element of the natural form beseeches for liberation.

The preposition "for" indicates beseeching on behalf of the body/external natural form, consistent with the spiritual sense that supplication is directed toward the liberation of the natural mind from bondage.

Parallel to GAP-32, the auxiliary "did" completes "the body did beseech," maintaining the repetitive liturgical pattern of the passage where each mention of the body/natural form is followed by an act of supplication.
The conjunction links two acts of supplication in sequence — beseeching and the Mother's own beseeching — maintaining the escalating pattern of prayer in this passage.
The pronoun "him" completes "she besought him" — the divine sphere of life beseeching the Father — consistent with the petition pattern established throughout the chapter (¶8, ¶10).
The phrase completes the purpose clause "in that they might be free," expressing the goal of the supplication — liberation from bondage — consistent with the spiritual sense of freedom from falsity.
The preposition "through" links the act of liberation to its agent — the Ambassador/Mediating Truth — expressing that freedom comes through the mediating power of divine truth.
The verb "came" describes the Ambassador's descent to accomplish liberation, connecting to the "and also" that follows to indicate additional acts of redemption.

The chapter's central motif of the divine "giver of ease" requires that the concluding act of this passage describe the bestowal of heavenly peace — "gave them ease" parallels the formulaic language used throughout (¶13, ¶14, ¶20).

The spiritual sense requires identifying the redeemed spirits in their restored state, and "He dwells with the living ones" describes the conjunction of the restored good with those who have received spiritual life — continuing from the preceding rescue narrative.

The verb "rests" completes the phrase describing eternal repose — "dwells with the living ones and rests for ever" — echoing ¶14's statement that the restoring power "has himself become rested, with him for ever."
The conjunction links the statement of eternal rest to the next clause about the first/primal state, continuing the narrative flow.

The phrase completes "the first Man was freed from the..." identifying the First Man (celestial will) as the one liberated, consistent with the chapter's entire arc of the First Man's descent into affliction and rescue.

"Affliction" is the chapter's primary term for the temptation-state from which the First Man is rescued (see ¶9, ¶10, ¶12, ¶14, ¶20), and the conjunction links this liberation to the bestowal of hope that follows.

The spiritual sense requires a description of the hope's nature — the assured expectation of eternal salvation — and "the hope of life" expresses this as the promise of spiritual life restored after liberation from the death-states of darkness.

The spiritual sense requires identifying whose will was perfected, and "the will of the Father" is the foundational divine purpose from which all entreaties proceed — paralleling the text's repeated references to the Father as the source of all granting.

The text later in ¶27 states "He granted the will of the elements," confirming that the will of the elements is a key concept in this passage; here it appears as the second will perfected alongside the Father's will.

The verb "fulfilled" connects the finding of light to the accomplishment of divine purpose, paralleling the chapter's pattern where each act of rescue fulfills the will that was petitioned (¶13, ¶21).

The text explicitly mentions "the will of the elements" later in the same paragraph, and the spiritual sense identifies the referent as the fundamental constituents of spiritual life — the elements whose will/desire is fulfilled by the divine power.

The verb describes what the Father had done regarding the will of the elements — "desired" avoids the tautology of "willed the will" and expresses the divine intention/longing that precedes the granting of the entreaty.

The phrase completes the granting of the elements' will with a statement of permanent rest, echoing the "rest and joy" formula used throughout the chapter (¶13, ¶14, ¶20) as the expression of heavenly peace.
"This first Man" refers to the First Man — the celestial will that underwent temptation — who was humbled and then made free, summarizing the entire arc of the chapter's first entreaty.
The conjunction links the liberation to what follows — the manifestation of divine power — continuing the paratactic narrative sequence.

The partial word gap requires a root that forms a word with "-ness"; "greatness" is a central Kephalaia term (Father of Greatness, power of his greatness) and the spiritual sense confirms that divine power/greatness is displayed before the forces of evil.
Paralleling GAP-46's "hope of life," this describes the nature of the hope received, and "to" transitions to the verb "reveal" that follows — "He received the hope of life to reveal..."
The preposition "through" connects the act of revelation to its agent — Jesus the Splendour — indicating that the hope of life is revealed through the fullness of divine truth in its radiance.

The phrase identifies the light power's origin in the Father, consistent with the chapter's repeated pattern of tracing all divine powers and entreaties back to the Father of Greatness as their source.

"The fathers of light" is established terminology in the chapter (see ¶17: "set it right by the fathers of light"), and the spiritual sense identifies the referent as the heavenly powers whose entreaty concludes the passage.
The chapter's closing formula of eternal fulfillment — "for ever" — appears throughout (¶14, ¶26, ¶27) and the spiritual sense requires a statement of eternal glorification to conclude the passage.
